name: Nyame
role: Supreme being associated with the sky
fun_fact: Nyame is also called Nyankopon, and many Akan prayers reach him through the abosom rather than directly.

name: Asase Yaa
role: Earth goddess who receives the dead and gives fertility
fun_fact: Her name means Earth Yaa, because Yaa is the day-name given to a girl born on Thursday, the day many communities set aside from farming.

name: Ananse
role: Spider trickster who wins and owns the stories
fun_fact: Ananse gave his name to anansesem, the Akan word for folktales, and to Anansi stories told across the Caribbean.

name: Onini the Python
role: Great python whom Ananse captures for Nyame
fun_fact: Onini is caught by flattery: Ananse gets him to stretch out beside a pole to prove his length, then ties him to it.

name: Osei Tutu
role: War leader who became the first Asantehene of the Asante union
fun_fact: Every later Asantehene traces the authority of the office back to the union Osei Tutu made with Okomfo Anokye.

name: Okomfo Anokye
role: Priest who called the Golden Stool down from the sky
fun_fact: Tradition says he planted a sword at Kumasi that no one has been able to pull out of the ground.

name: Akua'ba
role: Carved wooden doll carried by women hoping for a child
fun_fact: Akua'ba figures are among the best known works of African art, and the classic form has a flat, disc-shaped head.

name: Akua
role: Woman who first carried an akua'ba doll
fun_fact: Her name survives inside the doll's: akua'ba means Akua's child.

name: Sasabonsam
role: Forest monster who hangs in the highest trees
fun_fact: Sasabonsam is a boundary figure in Akan storytelling: it belongs to the untamed forest, not to the farms or the village.

name: Kwaku
role: Hunter who escapes Sasabonsam by his wits
fun_fact: Kwaku is a common Akan day-name for a boy born on Wednesday, so the hunter's name marks him as an ordinary man.
